title: AI-aided MRI detects local recurrence of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a multicenter cohort
summary: A 2.5D convolutional neural network and an nnU-Net contouring model were developed in a study of 6,916 patients at five hospitals. AUCs were 0.92 internally and 0.88 externally, with sensitivity of 79.5% and 74.3% and specificity of 91.0% and 92.8%. Sensitivity was comparable to MRI readers but lower than PET/CT, and in a randomized prospective cohort of 1,248 patients the AI group had higher sensitivity (78.6% vs 67.3%) that was not significant (P = 0.23).
ai_technology: 2.5D convolutional neural network for recurrence diagnosis and nnU-Net contouring model on MRI
organization: Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China

evidence.tested: Performance was compared with MRI and PET/CT in validation cohorts and in a randomized prospective cohort of 1,248 patients.
evidence.unknown: A significant benefit is unproven; the authors estimate 3,943 patients per arm would be needed. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN predicted and a nnU-Net visualized recurrence on MRI, used as an AI pre-inspector for radiologists.
